articles.title: Wait—Is Cyclospora Over? Here’s Whether You Can Finally Eat Your Leafy Greens Again Without Worrying
articles.content:
看来这场食源性疾病盛夏终于要结束了。难道不觉得每隔几天就有一起新的食品召回事件吗？墨西哥辣椒和鸡蛋含有沙门氏菌，蓝莓含有大肠杆菌，当然，包装沙拉（以及香菜和香菜）含有环孢子虫。

截至8月18日，环孢子虫疫情爆发以来，已有超过15,000人官方确诊感染，2人死亡。这次疫情与泰勒农场（Taylor Farms）在墨西哥中部种植的卷心菜有关，公司于7月17日发出自愿召回通知。自那以后，我们都在关注新闻，想知道这场夏季环孢子虫季节何时才能终结。

好消息是，快要到8月底了。这意味着危险已经过去吗？我们可以放心地撕开一包新鲜沙拉或者让塔可钟的厨师多放一些碎菜了吗？继续往下看，我将深入了解这场似乎永无止境的环孢子虫疫情的最新消息。

根据CDC的最新消息，截至8月18日，环孢子虫感染病例总数已达15,716例，其中约11,841例尚未通过实验室检测确认。有828人住院，2人死亡。

环孢子虫季节（是的，这是一个真实存在的季节）通常从5月1日持续到8月31日，因此随着6周的滞后时间过去，我们还可以预期更多病例的出现。

是的，永远如此。大多数情况下，彻底清洗绿叶蔬菜和其他水果蔬菜是保持安全的第一要务。

但是有一个例外，就是环孢子虫和其他寄生虫。不幸的是，它们无法被洗掉。你需要将产品加热到158华氏度（70摄氏度）才能降低患病风险。这对于煮豆子是没问题的，但对于卷心菜来说，就不太好了。这就是为什么必须注意召回通知，以便能丢弃涉及的产品。

对于其他未涉及疫情的产品，将其置于冷水下冲洗，并用手或蔬果刷擦洗以减少（但不能完全消除）食源性疾病的风险。始终洗手和清洁器具，丢弃外层叶子，以避免污染切割表面。

不是你的错。从5月1日到8月中旬，有15,716例环孢子虫感染病例向CDC报告。这比去年同期增加了10倍，去年5月1日至8月31日报告的病例不到1,200例。我们还看到沙门氏菌、李斯特菌、大肠杆菌和肉毒杆菌的疫情和召回事件。根据CNN报道，至少在过去五年中，我们从未经历过如此繁忙的食源性疾病季节。

专家将责任归咎于多种因素的综合作用。其中一个因素是特别炎热的夏季，为微生物繁殖提供了理想条件。另一个因素是预算削减。根据CBS新闻报道，在特朗普政府任期内，CDC失去了25%的员工，FDA失去了约20%。

曾于2015年至2023年主管FDA食品安全部门，现任耶鲁大学公共卫生学院兼职教授的苏珊·梅恩（Susan Mayne）告诉CBS新闻，美国曾有一个国家咨询委员会，帮助预防食品中的微生物污染。“该咨询委员会已被解散。”梅恩说，“我们过去会与墨西哥同行召开会议，讨论如何合作改善食品安全。整个团队都被解散了。”

这些削减不仅仅是一般的预算缩减，它们直接影响了像环孢子虫这样的食品寄生虫的追踪。食品网（FoodNet）是FDA、CDC和美国农业部联合运营的早期警报监测计划，缩减了从监测8种微生物到仅监测2种。猜猜看，环孢子虫没能入选。
articles.summary:
I can’t speak for you, but I am ready for our Summer of Foodborne Illness to be over. Doesn’t it seem like there’s a new recall every other day? Jalapeños and eggs have salmonella. Blueberries have E. coli. And, of course, bags of lettuce (and cilantro and parsley) have cyclospora.

As of Aug. 18, more than 15,000 people have been officially sickened, and two people have died since the cyclospora outbreak began. The outbreak was linked to Taylor Farms’ iceberg lettuce grown in central Mexico, and the company issued a voluntary recall on July 17. Since then, we’ve all been riveted to the news to learn just when the summer cyclospora season will finally draw to a merciful close.

Well, we’re almost to the end of August. Does that mean the coast is clear? Can we officially rip into a bag of fresh lettuce or ask the Taco Bell chef to pile on the shreds? Ahead, I’m digging into the latest news about the seemingly never-ending cyclospora outbreak. Read on to learn more.

Get Reader’s Digest’s Read Up newsletter for more food safety, cleaning, humor, travel, tech and fun facts all week long.

Is the cyclospora outbreak officially over?

I hesitate to say it’s over over, because the CDC is still investigating cyclospora outbreaks around the country, including two with unknown sources. These outbreaks are considered “ongoing.”

But as far as the recalled iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms is concerned, the CDC and the company confirm that the expiration dates on all recalled products have passed. That means you should not find any of the recalled lettuce on store shelves or served to you in a restaurant.

You may continue to hear about new cases of cyclosporiasis, however, because of reporting delays between illness onset and the CDC learning about the case. The typical lag time is about six weeks.

Are cases still being reported?

Yes. As of the latest CDC update, which came out on Aug. 18, cases are still being added to the total tally of cyclosporiasis illnesses, which stands at 15,716 laboratory-confirmed cases. About 11,841 additional illnesses have yet to be confirmed by lab tests. There have been 828 hospitalizations and two deaths.

The typical cyclospora season (yes, that’s a thing) runs from May 1 through Aug. 31, so we can expect more cases as that six-week lag time runs its course.

Should you still take precautions when washing produce?

Yes, always. Most of the time, thoroughly washing leafy greens and other fruits and veggies is the No. 1 thing you can do to stay safe.

There’s one caveat, and that’s cyclospora and other parasites. Unfortunately, they don’t wash off. You have to cook produce to 158 degrees Fahrenheit to reduce your risk of getting sick. That’s fine if you’re boiling green beans, but for iceberg lettuce? No thanks. That’s why it’s so important to pay attention to recalls so you can discard produce that’s been implicated.

For other produce that’s not involved in an outbreak, run it under cool running water and scrub with your hands or a produce brush to reduce (but not eliminate) your risk of foodborne illness. Always wash your hands and utensils, and discard outer leaves so you don’t contaminate your cutting surfaces.

Is it our imagination, or has there been a huge uptick in foodborne illnesses lately?

It’s not you. From May 1 through mid-August, 15,716 cases of cyclosporiasis were reported to the CDC. That’s more than 10 times the number from last year, when just under 1,200 cases were reported between May 1 and Aug. 31, 2025. We’ve also seen outbreaks and recalls involving salmonella, listeria, E. coli and botulism. According to CNN, we haven’t had such a busy foodborne illness season in at least five years.

Experts pin the blame on a combination of factors. One is a particularly hot summer, which provides ideal conditions for microorganisms to thrive. The other is budget cuts. Under the Trump administration, the CDC has lost 25% of its staff, and the FDA about 20%, according to CBS News.

Susan Mayne, who ran the food-safety department of the FDA from 2015 to 2023 and is now an adjunct professor at the Yale School of Public Health, told CBS News that the country used to have a national advisory committee to help prevent microbial contamination in food. “That advisory committee was disbanded,” Mayne said. “We used to convene meetings with our Mexican counterparts on how we can work together to improve food safety. That entire team was let go.”

These cuts aren’t just general budget trimming either. They directly impact the tracking of food parasites like cyclospora. FoodNet, an early-warning surveillance program jointly operated by the FDA, the CDC and the U.S. Department of Agriculture, scaled back from tracking eight microbes to just two. And you guessed it: Cyclospora didn’t make the cut.

Sources:

  • CDC: “Surveillance of Cyclosporiasis”
  • CDC: “Investigations of Foodborne Illness Outbreaks”
  • CDC: “FoodNet”
  • CBS News: “How Trump admin cuts have compromised food safety”
  • CNN: “It’s not just a gut feeling: Foodborne illness outbreaks are especially bad this summer”

articles.title: Prince George Won’t Be Allowed to Have This One Thing at Eton College
articles.content:
诚实地说，虽然成为全球焦点可能不是每个人的菜，但身为王室成员确实有一些特权。我们说的可不仅仅是住在豪华宫殿。这意味着你几乎可以拥有想要的一切——至少我们以为如此。

显然，王室生活并不总是表面看起来那么光鲜。威廉王子曾因能按按钮就能在他和祖母（即我们普通人眼中的伊丽莎白二世女王）在一起时立即获得冰淇淋而出名。但对于其他人，包括威廉的长子乔治王子来说，限制是他必须接受的部分。

实际上，乔治王子从9月开始在伊顿公学就读时，将面临非常严格的规则。这些规则包括不能拥有一件东西，而这是其他同龄男孩标准配置的——包括你的孩子。

那么，伊顿公学禁止乔治王子拥有什么东西呢？继续阅读来了解答案！

伊顿公学是英国最著名的私立寄宿学校之一。它位于温莎，距离温莎城堡仅一英里，距离威廉、凯特及其子女自2025年以来的居所弗罗斯特山庄约15分钟车程。伊顿公学由亨利六世于1440年创建。

最初，这所学校的目的是为70名贫困家庭的男孩提供教育。然而，几个世纪以来，它已成为王室成员、未来政治家、世界著名演员、音乐家、诗人和科学家的母校。

威廉和哈利都曾就读于伊顿公学，此外还有20位前任英国首相，包括鲍里斯·约翰逊和大卫·卡梅伦。演员休·劳里、汤姆·希德勒斯顿、埃迪·雷德梅恩以及作家乔治·奥威尔和詹姆斯·邦德创作者伊恩·弗莱明也曾在这里就读。

尽管校友名单令人印象深刻，年费也高达65,673英镑（约合88,700美元），但并不一定需要富裕才能进入这所精英学校。根据其官网，伊顿公学目前有约1,350名13至18岁的男生就读，其中2023-2024学年有18%的学生获得了财政援助。近100名学生完全免除了学费。

智能手机。

根据《电讯报》报道，伊顿公学禁止一年级学生使用带有互联网接入功能的手机。相反，学生们被发放了“砖头手机”，类似于我们曾经拥有的老式手机，只能发送和接收短信和电话。这些手机主要用于学生与家人在寄宿学校期间保持联系。

规则没有例外，甚至包括乔治，未来的国王。这项禁令旨在保护学生，根据学院网站的说法。但这一规则也符合时下趋势，因为越来越多的人渴望数字排毒（尽管我们不确定这包括一群青少年男孩）。

是的。没有智能手机并不意味着伊顿公学的学生与外界隔绝。校园内所有建筑都有Wi-Fi，学校图书馆也有台式计算机。每个学生在学年开始时还会获得一台iPad。

尽管如此，仍有一些限制：学校的网络是过滤和监控的，每个学生都必须参加电子安全讲座，并签署一份《可接受使用协议》，以规范其在校期间的在线活动。

你可能会觉得不可思议，但确实如此。在《不情愿的旅行者》节目中，威廉王子确认他的孩子们没有手机，他说他和凯特对这一点“非常严格”。然而，当他在2025年参加巴西地球奖时，他承认自己可能会重新考虑这一规则。

“确实很难。我们的孩子没有手机。”威尔士亲王说，然后补充说乔治可能会“在进入中学后……获得一部功能受限的手机”。威廉解释说，他和凯特想保护他们的孩子免于“在互联网上看到不该看到的东西”，但也承认他们无法永远保护他们。

因此，砖头手机可能是一个恰到好处的折中方案。

乔治王子的新校园以学术与丰富的课外活动相结合而自豪，包括体育、戏剧和音乐。所以谁知道？这位喜欢曲棍球的青少年王子（和他妈妈一样）可能很快成为一支体育队的新队长。伊顿公学还有超过80个社团供乔治加入，从环境协会到社会影响协会，还有各种体育和创业团体。

伊顿公学的学生住在24个不同的寄宿舍，每个舍房大约住55名学生，由宿舍长管理。因此，尽管乔治的学校距离家人住所仅一箭之遥，他仍然需要像其他学生一样住校。这对于这位青少年王子来说将是一个很大的改变，我们这样认为。他之前就读的兰布鲁克学校是一所日制学校，这意味着他白天在校，晚上回到父母身边。

尽管如此，作为第三顺位继承人，乔治已经习惯了变化和更高的责任。让我们回忆一下他12岁时开始生效的那个阴森可怖的规则。

威廉是迄今为止级别最高的就读过伊顿公学的王室成员。是戴安娜王妃在1995年决定将他送到这里。这个决定出乎意料地引发了争议，因为威廉的父亲查尔斯王子和祖父菲利普亲王都曾就读于苏格兰的戈登斯顿寄宿学校，威廉本应追随他们的脚步。

然而，年轻的王子似乎在温莎的学校度过了美好的时光，他能够享受一定程度的普通生活。当威廉18岁时离开伊顿公学时，他在一次采访中说：“我真的很享受能够在伊顿公学像其他学生一样生活。”

他的弟弟哈利似乎有更复杂的回忆。在他的书《备用品》中，他称自己在寄宿学校的第一天是“深刻的震惊”。他很难融入其他学生，而且因为威廉避免与他一起呆在一起而感到不满。但哈利并非一无所获。他确实享受伊顿公学的体育项目，甚至还参加了莎士比亚戏剧表演。
articles.summary:
Let’s be honest: While being in the spotlight around the clock might not be everyone’s cup of tea, being a royal does come with its fair share of perks. And we’re not just talking about living in fancy palaces. It also means you can have pretty much anything you want. Or so we thought.

Apparently, the life of a royal is not always what it seems. Yes, Prince William could famously order ice cream whenever he fancied just by pressing a button when he was with his grandma (better known as Queen Elizabeth II to us commoners). But for others, including William’s eldest son, restrictions are part of the deal.

It turns out that Prince George will have to follow some very strict rules when he starts at Eton, his new boarding school, this September. And these rules include not having one thing that’s pretty much standard for any other boy his age today—your own kids included.

So what item is banned by George’s new school? Scroll down to find out!

Get Reader’s Digest’s Read Up newsletter for more royals, cleaning, humor, travel, tech and fun facts all week long.

What is Eton, exactly?

Eton is one the most prestigious private boarding schools in the U.K. Located in Windsor, just a mile from Windsor Castle and about a 15-minute drive from Forest Lodge, where Kate, William and their kids have been living since 2025, Eton was founded by King Henry VI in 1440.

Originally, the school was established to educate 70 boys from disadvantaged backgrounds. Throughout the centuries, however, it has made a name for itself as the alma mater of royals and future politicians as well as world-famous actors, musicians, poets and scientists.

William and Harry both went to Eton, along with 20 former British prime ministers, including Boris Johnson and David Cameron. Actors Hugh Laurie, Tom Hiddleston and Eddie Redmayne and writers George Orwell and James Bond creator Ian Fleming also attended.

Despite the impressive alumni list—and the equally impressive fees of £65,673 ($88,700) per year—you don’t necessarily have to be wealthy to get into the elite school. According to its website, Eton currently teaches roughly 1,350 boys aged 13 to 18, and 18% of them received financial support during the 2023–2024 school year. Just under 100 students did not pay any fees at all.

What’s the one thing Prince George won’t be allowed to have there?

A smartphone.

Eton bans first-year students from having phones with internet access, according to the Telegraph. Instead, the students are given “brick phones,” similar to those old-school phones we all had back in the day, that can only send and receive text messages and calls. They’re mainly meant for students to stay in touch with their families during their time at the boarding school.

There are no exceptions to the rule, not even for George, the future king. The no-phone policy was implemented to protect the students, according to the college website. But the rule is also quite on trend, considering more and more people are longing for a digital detox these days (even though we’re not quite sure that includes a bunch of teenage boys).

Are students allowed any sort of online access?

Yes. Not having a smartphone doesn’t mean that Eton’s students are cut off from the outside world. Wi-Fi is available throughout the buildings, and there are desktop computers in the school’s library. Every student also receives an iPad at the beginning of the academic year.

That being said, there are still restrictions in place: The school’s network is filtered and monitored, and every pupil is required to attend lectures on e-safety and sign an Acceptable Use Agreement that governs their online activity at school.

Does Prince George have a phone?

Believe it or not, no. In an episode of The Reluctant Traveler with Eugene Levy, William confirmed that none of his kids have phones, saying that he and Kate were “very strict” about it. Yet, when visiting Brazil for the Earthshot Prize in 2025, he admitted he’d consider rethinking his own rule.

“It is really hard. Our children don’t have phones,” the Prince of Wales said, before adding that George will “maybe … have one with limited access” once he’s moved onto secondary school. William explained that he and Kate wanted to protect their kids from “seeing things on the internet that they shouldn’t,” but also acknowledged that they wouldn’t be able to shield them forever.

So a brick phone might be just the right compromise to start.

What else can George expect at Eton?

George’s new school prides itself on combining academics with tons of extracurricular activities, such as sports, drama and music. So who knows? The teenage royal, who plays hockey just like his mom, might soon be the new captain of a sports team. There are also more than 80 societies at Eton that he can join, ranging from the Environment Society to the Social Impact Society, plus a variety of sports and entrepreneurship groups.

Eton’s students live in 24 different boarding houses, each containing roughly 55 pupils and led by a house master. So while George’s school might be just a stone’s throw from his family home, he will still be required to sleep on-site like every other student. This will be quite a change for the teenage prince, we reckon. His former alma mater, Lambrook School in Berkshire, was a day school, meaning he spent the day there but went home to his parents in the evening.

That being said, as the third in line to the throne, George is used to change and heightened responsibility. Let’s remember for a second the morbid rule that kicked in when he turned 12.

What have William and Harry said about their time at Eton?

William is the most senior royal to date to have attended Eton. It was Princess Diana who decided to send him there in 1995. The move was surprisingly controversial, since both William’s father, Charles, and his grandfather, Prince Philip, had attended a boarding school in Gordonstoun, Scotland, and William was expected to follow in their footsteps.

However, it seems the young prince had a great time at his Windsor school, where he could enjoy a degree of normalcy. When William left Eton at the age of 18, he said in an interview, “I’ve really enjoyed being able to go about Eton as just another student.”

His brother, Harry, seems to have more mixed memories. In his book Spare, he called his first days at the boarding school a “profound shock.” He struggled to fit in with the other students, and he was upset that William avoided hanging out with him. But it wasn’t all bad for Harry. He did enjoy Eton’s sports programs, and he even took part in a Shakespearean play.
